model.name: SenseNova U1.5 8B MoT
model.description:
Generates higher-fidelity images with stronger composition, lighting, materials, fine detail, and efficient, coherent native 4K output.
Renders clearer Chinese and English text while following complex counts, layouts, spatial relationships, styles, and multi-part constraints.
Edits images reliably with better identity preservation and precise region- or object-level control via boxes, visual markers, and single or multiple references.

prompt:
Create a polished native-4K vertical infographic poster titled “THE ANATOMY OF A 15-MINUTE CITY” with the subtitle “Everything you need, closer to home.” Use a clean editorial grid, warm ivory background, deep navy typography, coral and teal accents, thin vector lines, realistic paper texture, precise spacing, and highly legible English and Chinese text. Render every quoted phrase exactly as written, without substitutions, omissions, duplicated letters, or invented text.
TOP STATISTICS:
“15 MIN” — “Maximum walk or bike time”
“6 ESSENTIAL NEEDS” — “Live • Work • Learn • Shop • Care • Play”
“30% FEWER CAR TRIPS” — “A practical target for compact neighborhoods”
“24/7 ACCESS” — “Safe, inclusive public space for everyone”
CENTER MAP:
Draw an isometric neighborhood map with a central home labeled “YOU ARE HERE / 你在这里”. Surround it with six color-coded zones:
“HEALTH / 健康” — “Clinic • Pharmacy • Mental health support”
“EDUCATION / 教育” — “School • Library • Skills center”
“FOOD / 食物” — “Market • Bakery • Community garden”
“WORK / 工作” — “Offices • Workshops • Coworking”
“MOBILITY / 出行” — “Bus • Metro • Bike share • Safe crossings”
“LEISURE / 休闲” — “Park • Sports • Culture • Café”
Add walking-time rings labeled:
“5-MINUTE CORE”
“10-MINUTE NEIGHBORHOOD”
“15-MINUTE COMMUNITY”
LEFT COLUMN — “WHY IT MATTERS”
“HEALTHIER DAYS” — “More walking, cleaner air, and easier access to care.”
“STRONGER COMMUNITIES” — “Local encounters build trust and belonging.”
“LOWER EMISSIONS” — “Short trips make active travel the easiest choice.”
“FAIRER ACCESS” — “Daily services should not depend on owning a car.”
“RESILIENT STREETS” — “Mixed-use districts adapt faster to change.”
RIGHT COLUMN — “DESIGN PRINCIPLES”
“01 — PROXIMITY” — “Place daily needs near homes.”
“02 — DIVERSITY” — “Mix housing, services, jobs, and culture.”
“03 — DENSITY” — “Support frequent transit and thriving local shops.”
“04 — UBIQUITY” — “Give every neighborhood equal-quality infrastructure.”
“05 — SAFETY” — “Design streets for children, elders, and disabled people.”
“06 — NATURE” — “Connect parks, shade, water, and biodiversity.”
BOTTOM TIMELINE — “ONE DAY, CLOSE TO HOME”
“07:30 — Walk to school”
“08:00 — Coffee from the corner bakery”
“09:00 — Work at the neighborhood studio”
“12:30 — Lunch in the community garden”
“15:30 — Visit the library”
“17:00 — Pick up groceries”
“18:30 — Exercise in the park”
“20:00 — Concert at the local cultural center”
FOOTER CHECKLIST — “IS YOUR NEIGHBORHOOD 15-MINUTE READY?”
“□ Continuous sidewalks”
“□ Protected cycle lanes”
“□ Frequent public transport”
“□ Affordable housing”
“□ Accessible healthcare”
“□ Local fresh food”
“□ Schools and childcare”
“□ Trees and public shade”
“□ Safe nighttime lighting”
“□ Welcoming public spaces”
Finish with the footer statement: “CLOSER SERVICES. SAFER STREETS. STRONGER COMMUNITIES.” and the small caption “A practical framework for healthier, more connected urban life.” Maintain perfect information hierarchy, crisp typography, accurate icons, balanced margins, and clearly separated sections.
